title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei responds: doesn’t oppose open-weight models, but fears Chinese AI
slides: Anthropic's CEO doesn't ban open-weight models outright—why?
His fear: Chinese AI could outpace Western safety standards.
Open weights may accelerate risks he can't control.
Your AI governance now needs geopolitical risk assessments.
Audit your model access: who truly benefits from openness?
thread_text:
Why not ban open weights?

Anthropic’s CEO says an outright ban could cede the AI race to China—where regulations are looser.

The real fear: Chinese AI

Beijing pours state funds into open models. Western safety norms may become optional.

Open weights = loose control

Once released, a model can’t be patched. Hostile actors tweak it without oversight.

Governance meets geopolitics

Your risk model now needs a China scenario. Failing that, you’re auditing blind.

Who in your org actually benefits from open weights? Map access and incentives this week.

instagram.caption:
Artificial intelligence from Beijing could reshape your safety protocols faster than your team can patch a model. 🚨

Anthropic’s CEO won't ban open-weight AI outright—because that would hand the race to China, where state-backed models face weaker Western safety standards. Once an open-weight model is public, hostile actors can tweak it with zero oversight.

Your governance now requires geopolitical risk assessments. 🧠

Audit who in your team truly benefits from openness this week—and map access. 🔍 Who would you trust to set the rules if your model got repurposed by an adversary?
